title: Managing Time During Interviews
description: Learn how to pace yourself across the 7-step framework so you cover the most important material within the interview time limit.

data.text: Most system design interviews last forty-five to sixty minutes. Without a mental clock, it is easy to spend too long on requirements and run out of time for the most interesting part: discussing trade-offs and deep-dive design. Time management is a skill you can practice before the interview.

terms.definition: A focused exploration of one component, such as the database schema or caching strategy.
A comparison of alternative designs and their costs in latency, complexity, or money.

rows: Align with interviewer on problem scope
Present core components and data flow

data.text: If you feel time pressure, move to the trade-off and deep-dive sections early. A high-level design with strong trade-offs is more impressive than a fully detailed design that never addresses bottlenecks. Ask the interviewer which area they want to explore if you run short on time.

data.title: Avoid the Detail Trap
data.text: Spending twenty minutes drawing every API endpoint is a common mistake. Focus on the data flow, storage, and scaling strategy instead.

data.title: Time Management Rules
points: Set internal checkpoints every ten to fifteen minutes.
Prioritize trade-offs over exhaustive API design.
If short on time, ask the interviewer which area to deep dive.
Leave time at the end for questions from the interviewer.
data.takeaway: Good pacing ensures you show your strongest work, not just your earliest work.
